name: The Hohenheim Love Plane

location.address: Exotischer Garten, Hohenheimer Gärten, Universität Hohenheim, Garbenstraße, 70599 Stuttgart-Hohenheim

access: In the free, publicly open Exotic Garden of the Hohenheimer Gärten (University of Hohenheim); open year-round, all day, no ticket. Parking on site.
transport: Stadtbahn U3 to Plieningen (terminus), about 300m walk
verify_notes: Known as the Hohenheim 'Liebesplatane' (love plane). Planted 1779 by Duke Carl Eugen of Württemberg, tradition says as a gesture for his future wife Franziska; the forked trunk (bifurcation at roughly 4m height) is read locally as 'two lovers, united in the trunk yet remaining two independent personalities in the canopy' (uni-hohenheim.de press release). Girth 7.70m measured at 1.3m stem height in December 2022 (nationalerbe-baeume.de). Height approx 34m, among the tallest plane trees in Germany. Designated a 'Nationalerbe-Baum' (National Heritage Tree, one of only ~100 in Germany) by the German Dendrological Society in May 2023. Also carries an official Naturdenkmal designation via LUBW (steckbrief id 2229013000033), which gives coordinates matching the other two sources exactly, treated here as a corroborating third source rather than one of the two required independents (register + nationalerbe-baeume.de + uni-hohenheim.de press release all agree). Habitat value noted for Juchtenkäfer (Eremit beetle, a protected saproxylic species), cavity-nesting birds, owls, dormice and bats. Inspected twice yearly by arborists with 'life-extending' care measures. No source this pass mentions storm damage (an unconfirmed WebSearch AI-summary snippet claimed storm Wiebke damage in the late 1990s; this did NOT appear in either fetched source page and is therefore dropped per the search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule).
